records.claimDecision: The authoritative Direct Method architecture is Loopback ULA + ctrld 1.5.7/DoH + NRPT + zapret/winws/WinDivert; the older Native-DoH handoff note is superseded.
Reuse the existing FreeNetHub Direct DPI method rather than add a duplicate method; replace only its obsolete service/adapter-DNS lifecycle.
FreeNetHub integrated lifecycle passed two independent Start/active/Stop cycles with exact cleanup and preserved adapter DNS, WinHTTP direct, ICS PID 5044, broad-route zero, and unrelated NRPT.
Source/live integration may be promoted only after package/installer parity; do not infer installed-release acceptance from source/live tests.

The two failing Direct-DPI product tests were stale: they still required the superseded adapter-DNS/ctrld-service lifecycle. The authoritative accepted R38 architecture preserves adapter DNS and runs ctrld foreground on an owned loopback ULA with a temporary owned NRPT catch-all. Tests were updated to assert the accepted ULA/NRPT ownership and exact pre/post DNS equality contract; runtime Start/Stop scripts were not changed.

records.context: R38 Linux-R11 rebase and public-evidence security reconciliation
records.claimDecision: R38 Direct Method was rebased onto the accepted Linux R11 origin/main without runtime-code conflict. The former two rollback-contract failures remain closed after rebase (Windows/source tests 145/145 PASS; Direct-DPI contract 5/5 PASS). A separate pre-push security gate then found machine-local Windows paths embedded in four R38 evidence files. The evidence was sanitized to project-relative or EXTERNAL provenance while retaining the underlying measurements; cycle evidence hashes and the integration acceptance references were updated. No Windows VPN, route, adapter DNS, Connect, Disconnect, or Direct Method lifecycle action was executed during this reconciliation.
evidenceSource: git rebase origin/main -> b9f1d14 before sanitation commit
records.rootCause: Raw live evidence serialized an absolute WinDivert driver PathName and the integration acceptance stored an absolute standalone-authority path. These are valid local provenance but invalid public-tree material.
records.prevention: Before any push or release, require tests/security_scan_public.py. Public evidence must encode project-owned paths relative to the repository and external authority as EXTERNAL:<project-relative-reference>; raw machine-local provenance remains private/local if needed. The existing security scan is the minimum sufficient regression guard; no duplicate gate is added.

records.context: Cross-platform deep audit - Linux R11 runtime defects
records.claimDecision: Live all-method audit on the actual Linux R11 install preserved the external tun0 and FreeNetHub cleanup but exposed two reproducible method-test defects: Tor benchmark treated status ok/state stopped as active and never started Tor; GOOL proxy upload used a 350KB sample that exceeded the 30s timeout on a slow but working path.
records.rootCause: Tor lifecycle predicate checked only tor_status.ok, although stopped is a valid ok status. Proxy upload benchmark used the same 350KB payload as direct access; GOOL uploaded at about 11.7KB/s and timed out before receiving HTTP 200, while a 100KB sample completed with HTTP 200.
records.prevention: Require Tor running state, not status-ok alone, before reusing Tor. Use a 100KB upload sample for proxy benchmarks and retain 350KB for direct/base. Keep explicit cleanup and physical-route preservation checks.

records.context: Cross-platform deep audit - Windows R38 protected active session
records.claimDecision: Windows R38 source/public-tree gates pass, and the final installer builds with frozen inputs, but the currently installed payload is older than the final R38 Windows source. A browser WARP FreeNetHub session is currently CONNECTED_HEALTHY, so force-closing the app or forcing installer promotion is intentionally deferred to preserve the user's active connection.
records.rootCause: The currently running installed app holds the product single-instance/app mutex and is actively carrying a browser WARP session. The protected installed payload predates final R38 FreeNetHub.ps1 and DirectDPI Start/Stop bytes.
records.prevention: Do not terminate or replace an active user session for release validation. Promote the hash-pinned installer only after the active FreeNetHub session is naturally stopped, then require exact installed parity and five-tab route-preserving smoke before public Windows R38 promotion.
